messages:
maya: Heads up — eu-west control plane warm-restart (~06:10 UTC) and since then apiserver 5xx spikes + leader swings. GPU attach jobs failing. Investigating.
sam: Any alerts/graphs? NAT/GW saturation maybe? Can you paste the error from attach-controller?
maya: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/eu-west1/dashboard/ctlplane
maya: snippet from metrics:
```
apiserver_request_total{code="503"} 1342
apiserver_request_duration_seconds_bucket{verb="WATCH",le="1"} 0.92
```
lia: Checked NAT gateway counters — SNAT port usage > 94% for cluster-eu-west1. Lots of TIME_WAIT sockets on node-proxies.
lia: `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide` shows kube-proxy flapping on 4 nodes
nora: That explains watch fanout causing connection explosion after leader swing. Controller-manager reconciles everything -> many API watchers reconnect -> SNAT blowout.
oncall: Impact: several GPU pod attaches failing with attach-controller errors, backlog growing. Customers hitting 503s. Need quick mitigation.
maya: Error from attach-controller logs:
```
E0901 06:15:12.123 attach_controller.go:87] attach failed: grpc: code = ResourceExhausted desc = NAT port exhaustion
```
sam: Can we throttle controller-manager reconciliation rate or reduce watch concurrency temporarily?
lia: We can flip kube-apiserver flags to reduce max inflight for watches and increase max-connections-per-client? Also kube-proxy keepalive tweak to reuse connections.
nora: Quick plan: 1) Pause autoscaler for GPU nodepool (stop more attaches). 2) Reduce apiserver `--max-requests-inflight` from 1000 -> 600 and enable `--request-timeout=30s` as a short-term. 3) Patch controller-manager client QPS/burst to 20/100. 4) Reconfigure NAT gateway to increase ephemeral ports if possible.
maya: Applying (2) and (3) as a canary on two control plane members now. Controller-manager config change (kubeconfig flags):
```
--kube-api-qps=20
--kube-api-burst=100
```
deploy-bot: configmap/ctlplane-flags updated for control-plane-canary; restarting apiserver-xx and controller-manager-yy (canary) :gear:
sam: After canary, apiserver 503 rate dropped ~60% on those members. NAT port usage fell ~10%.
lia: Still seeing attach errors on remaining nodes. Need cluster-wide changes or NAT port pool reallocation. I can bump conntrack and ephemeral port range on node pool as intermediate:
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=1500000
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 61000"
```
nora: Opening hotfix PR to default controller-manager client burst and add feature flag to reduce watch fanout for gpu CRDs. Also adding fallback to local CPU pool for attaches when attach controller returns ResourceExhausted.
maya: Good. For immediate customer relief I'm enabling regional fallback routing for gpu attaches so we don't hard-fail on attach errors.
oncall: Please document mitigation steps and timeline in incident board. We'll follow up with postmortem once stable.
maya: Thanks everyone — canary changes look promising. Will coordinate next steps and revert the temporary flags once NAT scaling is provisioned. :thumbsup:
